people.adam.relations: Husband of Eve. Father of Cain, Abel, and Seth.
people.adam.meaning: God puts him in the garden of Eden to work and keep it. God tells him not to eat from one tree. He eats the fruit that Eve gives him. God sends him out to farm the ground.
people.eve.relations: Wife of Adam. Mother of Cain, Abel, and Seth.
people.eve.meaning: The serpent talks with her, and she eats the fruit. She gives some to Adam. Adam names her Eve, the mother of all the living. She later names Seth as the child God gave in place of Abel.
people.cain.relations: Son of Adam and Eve. Brother of Abel. Father of the Enoch in Cain’s line.
people.cain.meaning: He farms the ground and brings an offering. God respects Abel’s offering and not his. He kills Abel in the field. God sends him away, and he lives in the land of Nod.
people.abel.meaning: He keeps sheep and brings an offering from his flock. God respects him and his offering. Cain kills him in the field. God says Abel’s blood cries from the ground.
people.enoch.relations: Son of Jared in Seth’s line. Father of Methuselah. Cain’s son Enoch is another man.
people.enoch.meaning: He walks with God for three hundred years after Methuselah’s birth. Then he is not found, for God takes him. Moses 6–7 gives him a larger part in LDS scripture.
people.noah.role: Builder of the ship in the flood
people.noah.relations: Son of Lamech. Father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
people.noah.meaning: God tells him to build a ship, and he does all that God commands. He takes his family and the animals inside. After the flood he builds an altar. God makes a covenant never to destroy the earth by flood again.
people.shem.relations: Brother of Ham and Japheth. Abram comes from his line.
people.shem.meaning: He and Japheth cover their father Noah without looking at him. Noah blesses the LORD, the God of Shem. Genesis 11 follows his line down to Terah and Abram.
people.ham.meaning: He sees his father Noah uncovered and tells his two brothers. Noah then curses Ham’s son Canaan, not Ham. The passage gives no support for racial slavery.
people.japheth.meaning: He helps Shem cover their father Noah. Noah asks God to enlarge Japheth. Genesis 10 lists his sons and the peoples that come from them.
people.nimrod.relations: Son of Cush. Grandson of Ham.
people.nimrod.meaning: He becomes a mighty one on the earth. People say, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.” His kingdom begins with Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in Shinar.
people.abraham.role: Man God calls to Canaan and promises a nation
people.abraham.meaning: God tells him to leave Haran, and he goes to Canaan. Out of fear he twice calls Sarah his sister. God promises him land and a son, and Sarah bears Isaac. He goes to offer Isaac, and the LORD’s angel stops him.
people.sarah.meaning: She has no child and gives Hagar to Abram. She then treats Hagar harshly. She laughs when she hears she will bear a son. She bears Isaac and tells Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away.
people.lot.meaning: He parts from Abram and chooses the plain of the Jordan near Sodom. Kings carry him off, and Abram rescues him. Two angels lead him out before Sodom is destroyed. His two daughters later make him drunk and bear his sons.
people.hagar.relations: Servant of Sarah. Mother of Ishmael, Abraham’s first son.
people.hagar.meaning: She conceives by Abram and runs from Sarai’s harsh treatment. The LORD’s angel finds her by a spring. She calls the LORD “a God who sees.” Later Abraham sends her away, and God hears her son’s voice.
people.ishmael.relations: Half-brother of Isaac. Father of twelve princes.
people.ishmael.meaning: The LORD’s angel tells Hagar to name him Ishmael. Abraham sends him away with Hagar, and God hears his voice. God promises to make him a great nation. He and Isaac later bury Abraham.
people.melchizedek.relations: Genesis names no family for him. He meets Abram after Lot’s rescue.
people.melchizedek.meaning: He brings out bread and wine after Abram rescues Lot. He blesses Abram and blesses God Most High. Abram gives him a tenth of all. LDS scripture says more about his work as priest.
people.isaac.meaning: God promises him to Abraham and Sarah, and Sarah bears him. Abraham binds him on an altar, and God provides a ram. He marries Rebekah and digs his father’s wells again. When he is old and cannot see, he blesses Jacob in place of Esau.
people.rebekah.relations: Daughter of Bethuel. Sister of Laban. Wife of Isaac.
people.rebekah.meaning: She draws water for Abraham’s servant and his camels. She agrees to go to Canaan and marry Isaac. She bears twins, Esau and Jacob, and loves Jacob. She dresses Jacob as Esau so that Isaac blesses him.
people.abimelech.role: King who deals with Abraham and Isaac
people.abimelech.relations: He deals with Abraham in Genesis 20–21. An Abimelech deals with Isaac in Genesis 26. Phicol leads his army.
people.abimelech.meaning: He takes Sarah, and God warns him in a dream. He gives her back and swears an oath with Abraham at Beersheba. In Genesis 26 an Abimelech learns that Rebekah is Isaac’s wife. Genesis does not say if this is the same king.
people.esau.meaning: He sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil stew. Jacob then takes his blessing, and Esau plans to kill him. Years later he runs to meet Jacob and kisses him. He settles in the hill country of Seir.
people.jacob.meaning: He buys Esau’s birthright and tricks Isaac to get the blessing. Laban then tricks him, and he works twenty years for Laban. He wrestles a man at night and is named Israel. In old age he goes to Egypt to see Joseph.
people.laban.relations: Father of Leah and Rachel. Jacob works for him.
people.laban.meaning: He welcomes Abraham’s servant and lets Rebekah go. He gives Jacob Leah in place of Rachel after seven years of work. Jacob says Laban changed his wages ten times. Laban chases Jacob to Gilead, and they make a covenant there.
people.leah.meaning: Laban gives her to Jacob in place of Rachel. Jacob loves Rachel more, and the LORD gives Leah children. She names Reuben for her pain and Judah for her praise. Jacob buries her in the cave of Machpelah.
people.rachel.meaning: Jacob loves her and works fourteen years for her and Leah. She has no child for years, then bears Joseph. She takes her father’s teraphim when the family leaves. She dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath.
people.bilhah.relations: Rachel’s servant. Mother of two of Jacob’s sons.
people.bilhah.meaning: Laban gives her to Rachel as a servant. Rachel gives her to Jacob, and she bears Dan and Naphtali. Rachel names both boys. Reuben later lies with her, and Genesis gives her no words.
people.zilpah.relations: Leah’s servant. Mother of two of Jacob’s sons.
people.zilpah.meaning: Laban gives her to Leah as a servant. Leah gives her to Jacob, and she bears Gad and Asher. Leah names both boys. Genesis gives Zilpah no words.
people.dinah.meaning: She goes out to see the daughters of the land. Shechem, son of Hamor, takes her and lies with her. Simeon and Levi kill the city’s men and take her from Shechem’s house. Genesis gives her no words.
people.joseph.role: Son sold into Egypt who later rules under Pharaoh
people.joseph.meaning: His brothers hate him and sell him, and he is taken to Egypt. Potiphar’s wife accuses him falsely, and he goes to prison. He explains Pharaoh’s dreams and stores grain for the famine. He feeds his family and tells his brothers God meant it for good.
people.judah.meaning: He tells his brothers to sell Joseph and not kill him. He keeps Tamar from his son Shelah, then says she is more righteous. He promises Jacob to bring Benjamin back. In Egypt he offers to stay as a slave in Benjamin’s place.
people.reuben.meaning: He lies with Bilhah, and his father hears of it. He tells his brothers not to kill Joseph and plans to bring him home. He offers his two sons as a pledge for Benjamin. Jacob says Reuben will not excel.
people.simeon.meaning: He and Levi kill the men of Shechem after Shechem defiles Dinah. Joseph later binds him and keeps him in Egypt. He goes free when the brothers bring Benjamin. Jacob curses the anger of Simeon and Levi.
people.levi.meaning: He and Simeon kill the men of Shechem and take Dinah away. Jacob says they have brought him trouble. In his last words Jacob curses their anger and says he will scatter them.
people.benjamin.relations: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Full brother of Joseph.
people.benjamin.meaning: Rachel dies at his birth and names him Benoni, but Jacob names him Benjamin. Jacob fears to send him to Egypt. Joseph’s cup is found in his sack. Judah offers to stay as a slave in his place.
people.tamar.role: Judah’s daughter-in-law who bears his twin sons
people.tamar.meaning: Judah sends her home and does not give her to his son Shelah. She veils herself, and Judah lies with her without knowing her. She keeps his signet, cords, and staff. When Judah sees them he says she is more righteous.
people.potiphar.meaning: He buys Joseph and puts him over his whole house. His wife says Joseph tried to lie with her. He grows angry and puts Joseph in the king’s prison.
people.pharaoh.relations: The Pharaoh of Genesis 12 deals with Abram and Sarai. A later Pharaoh deals with Joseph and Jacob.
people.pharaoh.meaning: In Genesis 12 a Pharaoh takes Sarai and then sends Abram away. In Joseph’s time a Pharaoh dreams of seven fat and seven thin cattle. He sets Joseph over Egypt and gives Jacob’s family land in Goshen. Genesis names no Pharaoh.
people.asenath.relations: Daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. Mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.
people.asenath.meaning: Pharaoh gives her to Joseph as a wife. She bears Manasseh and Ephraim before the famine. Genesis tells nothing else about her.
people.ephraim.meaning: He is born in Egypt before the famine. Jacob takes him as his own son. Jacob puts his right hand on Ephraim, the younger. Jacob says the younger brother will be greater.
people.manasseh.meaning: He is Joseph’s firstborn, born in Egypt. Jacob takes him as his own son. Jacob puts his left hand on Manasseh and his right on Ephraim. Joseph objects, but Jacob says Manasseh will also be great.
places.ur.summary: Terah’s son Haran dies in Ur of the Chaldees. Terah leaves Ur with Abram, Sarai, and Lot in Genesis 11. Southern Ur is a common choice for the site.
places.ur.limits: Scholars still debate which place Genesis means.
places.haran.summary: Terah’s family settles here, and Terah dies (Genesis 11). Abram leaves Haran for Canaan in Genesis 12. Jacob later flees here to Laban.
places.babel.summary: Nimrod’s kingdom begins at Babel in Genesis 10. In Genesis 11 people build a city and a tower in Shinar. The LORD confuses their language, and the city is named Babel.
places.babel.limits: Babylon is the usual choice for the city. No one has identified the tower.
places.ararat.summary: The ship rests on Ararat’s mountains in Genesis 8.
places.ararat.limits: The marker shows a broad mountain region, not one peak.
places.shechem.summary: Abram builds an altar here in Genesis 12. Jacob buys land here in Genesis 33. In Genesis 34 Simeon and Levi kill the men of the city. Joseph looks for his brothers here in Genesis 37.
places.bethel.summary: Abram builds an altar near Bethel in Genesis 12 and returns in Genesis 13. Jacob dreams here and names the place Bethel (Genesis 28). God sends Jacob back here in Genesis 35.
places.bethel.limits: Beitin is a common identification. The exact ancient site is not sure.
places.hebron.summary: Abram lives by the oaks of Mamre in Hebron (Genesis 13). Sarah dies here, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 23). Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are later buried in that cave.
places.hebron.limits: The marker shows Hebron. It does not prove where the burial cave is.
places.beersheba.summary: Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath here in Genesis 21. Isaac makes his own oath with Abimelech in Genesis 26. Jacob offers sacrifices here on his way to Egypt (Genesis 46).
places.beersheba.limits: The marker shows the area of the ancient town.
places.egypt.summary: Abram goes to Egypt in a famine (Genesis 12). Joseph is sold there and rises to rule under Pharaoh. Jacob’s family moves there in Genesis 46.
places.egypt.limits: The marker shows the whole region, not one city.
places.goshen.summary: Joseph settles Jacob’s family in Goshen in Genesis 46–47. Pharaoh calls it the best of the land.
places.goshen.limits: The marker shows a broad part of the delta. Goshen’s exact limits are unknown.
places.sodom.summary: Lot moves his tent as far as Sodom in Genesis 13. Abraham pleads for the city in Genesis 18. In Genesis 19 the LORD rains sulfur and fire on it.
places.sodom.limits: The site is disputed. The marker shows a region, not a known city.
places.zoar.summary: Lot asks to flee to this small city in Genesis 19. He reaches Zoar at sunrise, then leaves for the mountain.
places.zoar.limits: The exact site is not sure.
places.gerar.summary: Abraham stays in Gerar in Genesis 20, and Abimelech takes Sarah. Isaac stays here in Genesis 26, and herdsmen argue over his wells.
places.gerar.limits: Tell Haror is a proposed site. The marker is a rough guide.
places.beer-lahai-roi.summary: The LORD’s angel finds Hagar by a spring in Genesis 16. The well is then called Beer Lahai Roi. Isaac later lives near it.
places.beer-lahai-roi.limits: Its site is unknown. The marker shows only the Negev region.
places.moriah.summary: God sends Abraham to the land of Moriah to offer Isaac (Genesis 22). The LORD’s angel stops him there, and Abraham offers a ram.
places.moriah.limits: A later Bible book links Moriah with Jerusalem. Genesis gives no sure site.
places.salem.summary: Melchizedek, king of Salem, meets Abram in Genesis 14. He is priest of God Most High.
places.salem.limits: Tradition identifies Salem with Jerusalem. Genesis alone does not prove it.
places.dan.summary: Abram chases the kings who took Lot as far as Dan (Genesis 14).
places.dan.limits: The name Dan may come from a later time than Abram.
places.damascus.summary: Abram chases the kings to Hobah in Genesis 14. The text puts Hobah on the left hand of Damascus.
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows Damascus. Hobah’s exact site is unknown.
places.gilead.summary: Laban catches up with Jacob in the mountain of Gilead (Genesis 31). They heap up stones and make a covenant there.
places.gilead.limits: The marker shows a hill region, not one spot.
places.mahanaim.summary: God’s angels meet Jacob here in Genesis 32. Jacob says, “This is God’s army,” and names the place Mahanaim.
places.mahanaim.limits: The site is not sure. The marker shows the wider region.
places.penuel.summary: Jacob wrestles a man until dawn near the ford of the Jabbok (Genesis 32). He names the place Peniel. He then meets Esau in Genesis 33.
places.succoth.summary: Jacob builds a house and shelters for his livestock here in Genesis 33.
places.bethlehem.summary: Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath (Genesis 35). The text says Ephrath is also called Bethlehem.
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town. Traditions differ about where Rachel is buried.
places.edom.summary: Esau lives in the hill country of Seir in Genesis 36. The chapter lists his sons and the chiefs of Edom.
places.edom.limits: The marker shows a region, not a border.
places.dothan.summary: Joseph finds his brothers at Dothan in Genesis 37. They throw him into a pit and sell him.
places.adullam.summary: Judah visits Hirah, an Adullamite, in Genesis 38. Hirah later goes with Judah to Timnah.
places.timnah.summary: Judah goes up to Timnah to shear his sheep in Genesis 38. Tamar waits for him on the road there.
places.timnah.limits: More than one ancient site has this name. The right one is not sure.
places.canaan.summary: Jacob lives in Canaan during the famine. His sons travel from Canaan to Egypt for grain in Genesis 42–43. In Genesis 45 Joseph sends them back to bring Jacob.
places.canaan.limits: The marker shows a region, not a border.
sources.web.limits: Chapter notes describe the account. They do not prove every event in it.
sources.yale-creation.limits: This is a university reading, separate from LDS teaching. Scholars disagree about how Genesis was written. They also disagree about how much is history.
sources.yale-flood.limits: This is a university reading, separate from LDS teaching. Scholars disagree about how Genesis was written. They also disagree about how much is history.
sources.yale-ancestors.summary: Christine Hayes introduces ways to read the stories of the ancestors.
sources.yale-ancestors.limits: This is a university reading, separate from LDS teaching. Scholars disagree about how Genesis was written. They also disagree about how much is history.
sources.yale-patriarchs.limits: This is a university reading, separate from LDS teaching. Scholars disagree about how Genesis was written. They also disagree about how much is history.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.wiki-genesis.summary: Genesis starts with creation and the first people. It then follows the families of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. This overview helps explain how the book is built.
sources.dm-genesis.summary: McClellan discusses different creation accounts and older flood traditions. He states uncertainty about Babel’s possible sources. He also describes Genesis 49 as poetry kept inside a larger story.
sources.dm-genesis.limits: This is one scholar’s interpretation, separate from Church teaching. His proposed dates and his claims about scholarly agreement were not checked separately.
